questions.question: Which dancing form is classified as Ekaharya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam is the Indian classical dance form that is classified as Ekaharya**
 
• Ekaharya is a** technique in Bharatnatyam where a single dancer plays multiple roles in a single performance. **
 
• **Other features**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam is a popular dance form in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
 
• It is known for its storytelling, footwork, hand movements, facial expressions, and acrobatic dancing. 
 
• The Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur has been a center for Bharatnatyam since 1000 CE.
 
• The Tanjore Quartette is said to have been responsible for the current repertoire of Bharatnatyam in the early 19th century. 
 
• The Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikesvara is a primary text used to study the technique and grammar of body movement in Bharatnatyam
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi, Sattriya, and Kathak are all classical dances of India: 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• This dance originated in Odisha, India's easternmost state.
 
• It is primarily a dance for women, with postures that are similar to those found in temple sculptures. 
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• This dance is from Assam and is associated with the Sattras (Vaishnava maths or monasteries).
 
• It is governed by strict principles for footwork, hastamudras, aharyas, and music. 
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• This dance originated in Uttar Pradesh (U.P) in North India.
 
• The word Kathak means story, and dancers narrate stories through their expressions and eyes.

questions.question: Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra campaign was flagged off by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on November 15, 2023, at ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Khrunti, Jharkhand**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra** campaign was flagged off by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on **November 15, 2023**, from **Khunti, Jharkhand**. 
 
• This initiative was aimed at promoting the vision of a developed India by 2047, coinciding with the centenary of India’s independence.
 
• Along with the launch from Khunti, **multiple Information, Education and Communication (IEC) vans** were dispatched from various locations across the country. 
 
• These vans are designed to raise awareness about the government's development initiatives, encouraging public participation and engagement for national progress.
 
• Khunti is a significant location as it is associated with tribal heritage, and the launch in this region underscores the government’s commitment to uplifting tribal communities as part of its inclusive development agenda.
 
• The **Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra** is designed to promote the government’s vision of building a **self-reliant, developed, and prosperous India**.
 
• It emphasizes inclusivity and aims to involve people from all walks of life in contributing to the nation’s development.

questions.question: In the context of the Indian census, what is the definition of the literacy percentage?

options.text: The percentage of people aged seven and above, who can read and write in any language
The percentage of people with a college degree
The percentage of people who can read and write in English
The percentage of people who can perform basic arithmetic calculations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the Indian census, *l**iteracy rate***** is a measure of the proportion of people in a population who have basic reading and writing skills in any language.**
 
• This definition does not require fluency or advanced literacy skills but simply the ability to read and write with comprehension.
 
• T**he literacy rate considers individuals aged seven years and above.**
 
• This age threshold is set because, by this age, most children have started schooling and are expected to acquire basic reading and writing skills
 
• Literacy does not imply having a college degree or advanced education
 
• **It simply means the ability to read and write with understanding.**
 
• The l**iteracy rate counts people who can read and write in any language, not necessarily English or Hindi.**
 
• This inclusivity is important in a multilingual country like India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principles of State Policy mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
Uniform civil code for the citizens
Promotion of international peace and security

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Separation of the legislature from the executive**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Separation of the legislature from the executive**
 
• This is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The separation of powers between the legislature and executive is a part of the general structure of governance but is not specifically mentioned as a Directive Principle of State Policy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Part of the Directive Principles:

questions.question: Where was the first Asian Games held in 1951?
questions.solution:

• The **first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India in 1951**
 
• It was **Held on March 8–11, 1951** 
 
• It was held in **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium,** also known as the National Stadium 
 
• **489 athletes from 11 Asian countries competed in 57 events across eight sports,** including association football, athletics, basketball, cycling, swimming, and weightlifting

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, **also known as "Frontier Gandhi," was the founder of the *Khudai Khidmatgars*, or "Servants of God.**"
 
• This **movement was a non-violent resistance organization formed in the North-West Frontier Province** (present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan) to fight British colonial rule.
 
• **Ghaffar Khan was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi** and a prominent advocate of non-violence.
 
• The Khudai Khidmatgars promoted peace, social reform, and independence from British rule, relying on peaceful protests and social activism rather than armed struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sayyid Ahmed Khan:**

 
 
• He was a prominent 19th-century Muslim scholar and reformer in British India, known for founding the Aligarh Movement and Aligarh Muslim University to promote modern education among Muslims. 
 
 
 
• **Maulana Azad:**
 
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a senior leader in the Indian independence movement and the first Education Minister of independent India. 
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**:
 
 
• Jinnah was the leader of the All India Muslim League and later the founder of Pakistan.
 
• He played a significant role in the political landscape of British India but was not involved with the Khudai Khidmatgars movement.

questions.question: According to the data of 2011 - 12, which of the following is the poverty rate of bihar ? (approximate)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**33.7%**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **2011-12, 33.7 percent of the population of Bihar was living in poverty.**
 
• C**ompared to India's 25.7 percent rural poverty, 13.7 percent urban poverty, and 21.9 percent overall poverty rate in 2011-12**, these numbers are astronomical.
 
• This was reflective of several factors, including limited access to quality education, healthcare, infrastructure, and economic opportunities in the state.
 
• **Factors Contributing to Bihar's Higher Poverty Rate**:
 
 
• **Agriculture-based economy:** Bihar’s economy is primarily agriculture-based, and it has faced issues like low agricultural productivity, poor irrigation systems, and vulnerability to natural disasters like floods.
 
• **Poor infrastructure: **Bihar lags behind other states in terms of infrastructure development, including transportation, health services, and education.
 
• **Low industrialization: **Unlike some other states, Bihar has had limited industrial growth, which has contributed to fewer job opportunities outside of agriculture.
 
• **Social challenges:** Issues like low literacy rates, gender inequality, and caste-based disparities also exacerbate poverty in the state.

questions.question: With respect to economic planning in India, the Bombay Plan was published in how many parts ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bombay Plan came out in two parts the first, in early 1944 and the second, later that year.

 
 
• By 1944, World War II was winding down and Indian independence was around the corner. It was in this political backdrop that the country’s top industrialists decided to get together and prepare a plan for the economic development of independent India.
 
• It laid out the roadmap for India’s development after independence.
 
• It envisaged three Five-Year Plans, after which the economy would revert to a free-market model.
 
• The industrialists envisioned a major role for the state in the building of the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Economic planning refers to the actions of policy measures that are to be followed in the future, in pursuance of pre-determined objectives.

 
 
• Planning Commission now renamed as NITI Aayog defines Economic planning as the utilization of a country's resources for developmental activities.
 
 
 
• Objectives of Planning:
 
 
• The high rate of growth
 
• Modernization
 
• Economic Self-reliance
 
• Equity
 
• Economic stability
 
 
 
• The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 by a simple resolution of the Government of India.
 
 
• It had an advisory role and its recommendations become effective only when the Union Cabinet approved them.
 
• Minister of State for Planning (Independent Charge): Rao Inderjit Singh (as of Feb 2021)
 
 
 
• Purpose of Planning Commission: The commission’s original mandate was to raise the standard of living of ordinary Indians.
 
 
• ​By efficiently exploiting the country’s material and human resources, boosting production, and creating employment opportunities for all.

questions.question: Which dance style does Geeta Mahlik have a reputation for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Odissi dance form derives its name from the Odra Nritya mentioned in the Natya Shastra.
 
• This dance was primarily practised by the maharis and was patronised by Kharavela.
 
• Guru Pankaj Charn Das was a famous proponent of this dance.
 
• The earliest trace of this dance form was found in the Udaygiri-Khandagiri caves in Odisha.
 
• The variants of this dance form are Gotipua and Nartala, which is the court dance.
 
• The Tribhanga posture and mudras or hand gestures are the most important feature of Odissi.
 
• One of the popular themes of this dance form is the spiritual love of Radha and Krishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Mangalacharan" refers to the opening piece or invocation performed at the beginning of a dance recital or musical performance.
 
• The purpose of Mangalacharan is to invoke the blessings of the divine, seek auspiciousness.
 
• It often includes rhythmic footwork, expressive gestures, and melodic elements.
 
• Mangalacharan serves as a tribute to the gods and goddesses, as well as a way to express gratitude.

 
• Important Mudras of classical Odissi dance

 
 
• Pataka
 
• Ardhapataka
 
• Arala
 
• Suchi
 
• Shukachanchu
 
• Alapadma
 
• Ardha Chandra
 
• Kapitha
 
• Katakamukha
 
• Hansasya hastasPallava
 
• Keshabandha

questions.question: Which government department is responsible for implementing the VAIBHAV Fellowship Scheme?

questions.question: In which of the following Schedule of the Indian Constitution the 'Concurrent List' is given?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In respect of matters on which both the Parliament and the state legislatures have the power of legislation (i.e., the subjects enumerated in the Concurrent List), the executive power rests with the states except when a Constitutional provision or a parliamentary law specifically confers it on the Centre.
 
• Constitution confers executive power of a subject in the Concurrent List to the State Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Concurrent List:

 
 
• There are 52 (Originally 47) items currently on the list: This includes items that are under the joint domain of the Union as well as the respective States. However, given that there can be conflict when it comes to laws passed by Parliament and state legislatures on the same subject, the Constitution provides for a central law to override state law.
 
 
 
• Union List:
 
 
• The Union List is a list of 100 (Originally 97) numbered items as provided in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The Union Government or the Parliament of India has exclusive power to legislate on matters relating to these items.
 
 
 
• State List:
 
 
• The State List is a list of 61 (Originally 66) items in the Schedule Seven to the Constitution of India. The respective state governments have exclusive power to legislate on matters relating to these items.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The founder of the Mauryan dynasty, Chandragupta united the Indian subcontinent in the 4th century BC.
 
• After his political and military unification, he sought out monasticism and lived as a Jain.
 
• His court advisor and Kautilya was also known for his cunning statecraft and expansionary mindset.
 
• The two of them created an empire rarely rivaled in Indian history.

 
• The capital of Chandragupta's empire was Pataliputra near the Ganges river in northeastern India.
 
 
• A description of the city in the time of Chandragupta comes from the Greek traveler Megasthenes.
 
• It was known for being one of the largest cities in the world at the time of the Mauryan empire.
 
• The shape of the city was a parallelogram and apparently had 64 gates in its wooden walls.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• He was also known as Devanam Priyadasi.
 
• Ashoka invaded Kalinga in 261 B.C., in what is famously known as the Kalinga War.
 
• After witnessing the massive loss of life and suffering during the Kalinga War, he decided to end military conquests and converted to Buddhism.
 
• Ashoka promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia, becoming a significant patron of the religion.
 
• He was the first king in Indian history to document his achievements and messages on stones, known as Rock Edicts.
 
• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was built during Ashoka’s reign to commemorate the spread of Buddhism.

 
• Major Rock Edict 13 provides detailed information about his Kalinga War.
 
• There are a total of fourteen Major Rock Edicts.
 
• The two Kalinga Edicts are located in the newly conquered Kalinga territory.
 
• Major Pillar Edicts were erected in important cities to spread Ashoka’s messages.
 
• In addition to Major Rock Edicts, there are Minor Rock Edicts and Minor Pillar Edicts.
 
• Kalinga War
 
 
• Ashoka, the son of the Mauryan emperor Bindusara and grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, ascended the throne of Magadha in 273 B.C.
 
• Following the expansionist tradition of his ancestors, Ashoka sought to expand his empire further.
 
• In the 12th year of his reign, he sent a message to Kalinga (present-day Odisha) asking for its submission to the Mauryan empire. The Kalingaraj, however, refused to surrender.
 
• The Kalinga War was fought on the Dhauli hills along the banks of the Daya River.
 
• In 261 B.C., Ashoka led a vast army against Kalinga.
 
• The fiercely independent people of Kalinga mounted a strong defense against the Mauryan forces.
 
• Despite their determination and courage, the limited forces of Kalinga were no match for the massive Magadha army.
 
• The people of Kalinga displayed remarkable valor, nearly securing victory on several occasions.
 
• Ultimately, Ashoka's forces prevailed, but at an enormous cost to life and property. The entire region of Kalinga was left devastated.
 
• Ashoka’s 13th Rock Edict vividly describes the horrors and bloodshed of the Kalinga War.
 
• In about 263 B.C., after reflecting on the war’s destruction, Ashoka embraced Buddhism under the guidance of the monk Moggaliputta Tissa, who became his mentor.

questions.question: National Sport of Pakistan is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Field Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The game of field hockey was originally brought to Pakistan during the British Raj, and like cricket, became a popular sport among the local population.
 
• The Pakistan Hockey Federation came into being in 1948, following the independence of Pakistan in 1947.
 
• When Pakistan first won the Olympics gold in 1960, hockey was officially declared Pakistan's National Sport. 
 
• The Pakistan national team has been ranked as the number 1 team in the world in both 2000 and 2001 by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).

Thus, the national sport of Pakistan is Hockey.__
